anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

pass_a_gloss: For the one hearing about Christ and believing, this one has taken Christ, but he does not sacrifice him and chew unless five days have first passed; for there being five senses of the human, unless Christ come to be in each of them, he would not be able to be sacrificed and, having been roasted, be eaten.
pass_b_english: For the one who hears about Christ and believes — this one has taken Christ. But he does not sacrifice him and chew him unless five days have first passed. For since a human being has five senses, unless Christ comes to be in each of them, he could not be sacrificed and, having been roasted, be eaten.
source_text: Ὁ γὰρ ἀκούων περὶ Χ(ριστο)ῦ καὶ πιστεύων, οὗτος ἔλαβεν τὸν Χ(ριστό)ν, οὐ πρότερον δὲ θύει αὐτὸν καὶ τρώγει μὴ οὐχὶ πρότερον διαγενομένων ἡμερῶν πέντε· πέντε γὰρ οὐσῶν αἰσθήσεων τῶν τοῦ ἀν(θρώπ)ου, εἰ μὴ ἐν ἑκάστῃ αὐτῶν γένηται Χ(ριστό)ς, οὐκ ἂν δύνηται τυθῆναι καὶ ὀπτηθεὶς βρωθῆναι.
